(This evening through Monday)...
Issued at 242 PM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

Tonight.

The short term period will be characterized by anomalous warmth and 
increasing low level moisture ahead of an approaching central US 
trough. For tonight, the main forecast challenge relies on low level 
saturation and stratus trends. Model soundings and HREF 
probabilities indicate a persistent subsidence inversion aloft 
trapping boundary layer moisture. This will result in widespread 
stratus overnight. With weak forcing and lack of deep moisture, 
precipitation will be mostly limited to patchy drizzle and even this 
should end no later than midnight. Overnight lows will remain quite 
mild, generally in the middle 50s, due to the blanket of stratus and 
steady southerly surface flow.

Tuesday and Wednesday.

A deep upper level trough positioned over portions of the Great 
Plains and Rockies Monday will continue to amplify and eject towards 
the upper Midwest. In response, a tightening pressure gradient and 
subsequent height/pressure falls will aid in sustaining 35-40 kt of 
southerly flow at 850mb, transporting unseasonably warm, moist air 
from the Gulf across Indiana tomorrow. Strong WAA and vertical 
mixing supports near-record high temperatures in the mid to upper 
70s. However, a trailing cold front approaching from the west may 
provide a small amount of synoptic ascent during the daytime for the 
development of a few mid-to-high level clouds that could hinder high 
temperatures by a few degrees, and prevent any records from being 
broken.  

By Tuesday evening, the trailing cold front associated with the 
trough will be approaching areas to the west bringing with it a thin 
corridor of 60+ dew points along the leading edge. Strong isentropic 
ascent in the warm sector, PWAT values ~1.5 in slightly exceeding 
the 99th percentile for early November will support the development 
of widespread rain and thunderstorms in Illinois that will traverse 
into Indiana with time. Despite 50-60 kts of effective bulk shear, 
near-zero convective instability will preclude any widespread severe 
threat. However, a damaging wind gust or two cannot be ruled out due 
to 50-55 kt winds just above the surface.

In addition, the CAMs are indicating the potential of a dry air 
intrusion to occur as the cold front passes through our area. In 
turn, combined with very limited instability, convection, and 
consequently rain rates, should weaken as the cold front traverses 
across Indiana. As a result, rainfall totals could range anywhere 
from 0.3-0.6 in, with areas in southern Indiana having the best 
chance for higher rainfall amounts where less of the dry air may 
preclude totals. However, in the event where the dry air intrusion 
may be weaker or training of convective cells occurs, rainfall 
totals could be as high as 1.5 in. Any flash flood potential will be 
mitigated due to the onset of dry soil conditions over the last 
month. 

Once the cold front traverses the region Tuesday night, Wednesday 
will bring light residual shower activity in the CAA region behind 
the cold front, and more seasonable air with highs reaching into the 
low 60s and lows reaching into the mid 40s.

Wednesday Night Through Monday.

Broad cyclonic flow and a cold core aloft may allow for lingering 
stratocumulus through Thursday, but sensible weather will remain 
dry. Highs will retreat into the low 60s on Thursday. Heading into 
Friday and the weekend, ensemble guidance paints a high confidence 
picture of a pattern shift toward more seasonable November weather. 
Surface high pressure will slowly build eastward out of the Plains 
while persistent northwest flow aloft dominates. Thermal profiles 
highlight 850mb temperatures falling near or slightly below 0C. This 
CAA regime will keep daytime highs suppressed in the 50s Friday 
through Monday, with overnight lows dipping into the 30s and 40s. A 
few weak shortwaves embedded within the northwest flow may pass 
through the Great Lakes over the weekend, but moisture return looks 
largely cut off by the Gulf of Mexico trajectory, keeping 
precipitation chances minimal. We will maintain a largely dry 
forecast through Monday with near normal temperatures.
